chapter: Suntaug Lake Inn and Duke Ellington's band
title: Duke's show 'My People' in Chicago and Detroit
summary: He describes 'My People', the education of the Negro through music, which he copied, and the huge crowds in Detroit.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: and I said, hey, what are you going to do with this, and he said nothing, but in 1963 he went to Chicago and included -- he made My People, that was the show and in that show was 'Black, Brown and Beige.' He had the people coming from the pit, they were in rags, my people, our people in rags coming up and then at the end, they were doctors, and lawyers and everything.
I never saw that show, that must have been beautiful. You copied that.

Yeah. Man, I used to copy and run out and listen to the shows, copy and listen to the shows and I said to Duke, you know, this should be in the World's Fair, you should take this out to the World's Fair. Never got there. That was a show, I think it was one of the greatest shows I have ever seen, so the topic was Negro, see.
What was the name of that?

My People. It was the education of the Negro through music. And he developed it and oh, it was beautiful and the last thing was 'What is Color? What is Virtue?' He developed that thing, he was working over in Detroit and he come over and fix a part and go back to the show, to his show, when we was in Detroit. That lasted -- we'd go on -- and I'd have to go out in the lobby and I said tell the band leader, don't go until I tell you, because the people are lined out there coming into the show. They would come there

two and three times a week to see that show. Butterbeans and Susie they were there looked like every day and Alice,oh, what's her name, the Whitman sisters, they were there all the time. That was a great show.
You'd have three and four thousand people at that show.
